Created the discussion task:

- `kanban/discussion/2026-09-01-refine-history-index-sidebar.md`

The document records:

- Hide the index in rows; show it in the context menu.
- Add Check out to each row.
- Preserve single-line, single-branch, oldest-to-newest ordering and follow-latest behavior.
- Do not use TurnMarker; use Assistant Final to mark the end of a turn.
- Candidate content projections for all nine current entry types.
- Shared rules for images, empty content, line breaks, truncation, and loading failures.
- Boundaries requiring adjustment between History Index generations and existing revert-target validation.
- Checkout availability, confirmation flow, and scrolling after success.

Only the discussion document was created; no implementation was changed. `git diff --check` passed.

Most importantly, show only the message content by default, not its type. The sidebar has very limited horizontal space, so save as much as possible. Only on hover should a popup show the type and full content. We can also use color to represent the message type, making previews much more informative.

questions.question: Which parts of History Index should use the type color?

options.label: Node and content (Recommended)
options.description: Color the entire preview consistently for quick recognition without using extra horizontal space.

options.label: Node only
options.description: Keep a uniform foreground color for the text: visually restrained, but the type is less noticeable.

options.label: Content only
options.description: Keep the branch line in a uniform color and encode the type in the text.

The basic presentation is now agreed:

- Rows show single-line content only, without the type, role, or index.
- The single-branch graph and content share the same type color.
- Content beyond the available width uses an ellipsis.
- The hover popup shows:
  - The full type name.
  - The full content, preserving paragraphs.
- The hover popup does not show the index.
- The index appears only in the context menu.

Approximate appearance:

```text
┌● Please review this implementation...
├● I'll check the data structures and call chain...
└● Implementation complete; the relevant tests passed...
```

On hover:

```text
Assistant Final

Implementation is complete and the relevant tests passed.
This is the full message content, not truncated to the sidebar width...
```

The color scope is also confirmed: color the single-branch graph and content together. Next, decide the exact colors and content-summary rules for each type.

Request user input should show only the questions, with everything else visible on hover. Update plan should show only the last plan item that is not pending. Check out is not a destructive revert: it only scrolls the conversation history to the corresponding position.

Corrected the definitions in the task document:

- Request user input
  - The default row shows only each question's question text.
  - Do not show headers, options, answers, results, or errors.
  - Hover shows the full questions, options, answers, and results.

- Plan update
  - The default row shows the last item whose status != StepStatus.Pending.
  - Do not show the explanation, other items, or a status summary.
  - Hover shows the explanation and complete plan snapshot.
  - The fallback when every item is Pending still needs a decision.

- Check out
  - Pure navigation.
  - Only load and scroll the main conversation History to the corresponding storage index.
  - Do not call revert.
  - Do not truncate storage.
  - Do not change Agent state or the History Index generation.
  - Do not show a destructive confirmation dialog.
  - Do not reuse the canReplaceHistory constraint.
  - Do not change the History Index's own scroll position or follow-latest state.
